title: Diophantine Equations, SFFT, Bezout & Floor Functions

sections.heading: Diophantine Equations, SFFT, Bezout & Floor Functions Practice Exercises

questions.q: How many ordered pairs of POSITIVE integers \( (x, y) \) satisfy the bilinear Diophantine equation \[ xy + 1x + 2y = 10 \] (corresponding to positive lattice points on the plotted hyperbola)?
questions.answer: Add \( 1\cdot 2 = 2 \) to both sides (SFFT): \( (x + 2)(y + 1) = 10 + 2 = 12 \). For \( x, y \ge 1 \), we need \( d = x + 2 \ge 3 \) and \( 12/d = y + 1 \ge 2 \). Counting divisors \( d \mid 12 \) satisfying both inequalities yields exactly \( 3 \) positive integer pairs.

questions.q: How many ordered pairs of POSITIVE integers \( (x, y) \) satisfy the bilinear Diophantine equation \[ xy + 2x + 3y = 18 \] (corresponding to positive lattice points on the plotted hyperbola)?
questions.answer: Add \( 2\cdot 3 = 6 \) to both sides (SFFT): \( (x + 3)(y + 2) = 18 + 6 = 24 \). For \( x, y \ge 1 \), we need \( d = x + 3 \ge 4 \) and \( 24/d = y + 2 \ge 3 \). Counting divisors \( d \mid 24 \) satisfying both inequalities yields exactly \( 3 \) positive integer pairs.

questions.q: How many ordered pairs of POSITIVE integers \( (x, y) \) satisfy the bilinear Diophantine equation \[ xy + 1x + 3y = 17 \] (corresponding to positive lattice points on the plotted hyperbola)?
questions.answer: Add \( 1\cdot 3 = 3 \) to both sides (SFFT): \( (x + 3)(y + 1) = 17 + 3 = 20 \). For \( x, y \ge 1 \), we need \( d = x + 3 \ge 4 \) and \( 20/d = y + 1 \ge 2 \). Counting divisors \( d \mid 20 \) satisfying both inequalities yields exactly \( 3 \) positive integer pairs.

questions.q: How many ordered pairs of POSITIVE integers \( (x, y) \) satisfy the bilinear Diophantine equation \[ xy + 2x + 5y = 26 \] (corresponding to positive lattice points on the plotted hyperbola)?
questions.answer: Add \( 2\cdot 5 = 10 \) to both sides (SFFT): \( (x + 5)(y + 2) = 26 + 10 = 36 \). For \( x, y \ge 1 \), we need \( d = x + 5 \ge 6 \) and \( 36/d = y + 2 \ge 3 \). Counting divisors \( d \mid 36 \) satisfying both inequalities yields exactly \( 3 \) positive integer pairs.

questions.q: How many ordered pairs of POSITIVE integers \( (x, y) \) satisfy the unit-fraction equation \[ \frac{1}{x} + \frac{1}{y} = \frac{1}{6}? \]
questions.answer: Clearing denominators gives \( 6(x + y) = xy \iff xy - 6x - 6y = 0 \). Adding \( 6^2 = 36 \) via SFFT gives \( (x - 6)(y - 6) = 36 \). Since \( x, y > 6 \) for all positive solutions, \( x - 6 \) ranges bijectively over all positive divisors of \( 6^2 = 36 \), giving \( \tau(36) = 9 \) ordered pairs.

questions.q: Find the LARGEST positive integer \( n \) such that \( n + 2 \) divides \( n^2 + 3n + 15 \).
questions.answer: Perform polynomial division by \( n + 2 \): \( n^2 + 3n + 15 = (n + 2)(n + 1) + (2^2 - 3(2) + 15) = (n + 2)(n + 1) + 13 \). Thus \( (n + 2) \mid (n^2 + 3n + 15) \iff (n + 2) \mid 13 \). The largest divisor of \( 13 \) is \( 13 \) itself, giving \( n + 2 = 13 \implies n = 11 \).

questions.q: Find the LARGEST positive integer \( n \) such that \( n + 3 \) divides \( n^2 + 3n + 17 \).
questions.answer: Perform polynomial division by \( n + 3 \): \( n^2 + 3n + 17 = (n + 3)(n + 0) + (3^2 - 3(3) + 17) = (n + 3)(n + 0) + 17 \). Thus \( (n + 3) \mid (n^2 + 3n + 17) \iff (n + 3) \mid 17 \). The largest divisor of \( 17 \) is \( 17 \) itself, giving \( n + 3 = 17 \implies n = 14 \).

questions.q: Find the LARGEST positive integer \( n \) such that \( n + 4 \) divides \( n^2 + 3n + 19 \).
questions.answer: Perform polynomial division by \( n + 4 \): \( n^2 + 3n + 19 = (n + 4)(n + -1) + (4^2 - 3(4) + 19) = (n + 4)(n - 1) + 23 \). Thus \( (n + 4) \mid (n^2 + 3n + 19) \iff (n + 4) \mid 23 \). The largest divisor of \( 23 \) is \( 23 \) itself, giving \( n + 4 = 23 \implies n = 19 \).

questions.q: Find the LARGEST positive integer \( n \) such that \( n + 5 \) divides \( n^2 + 3n + 21 \).
questions.answer: Perform polynomial division by \( n + 5 \): \( n^2 + 3n + 21 = (n + 5)(n + -2) + (5^2 - 3(5) + 21) = (n + 5)(n - 2) + 31 \). Thus \( (n + 5) \mid (n^2 + 3n + 21) \iff (n + 5) \mid 31 \). The largest divisor of \( 31 \) is \( 31 \) itself, giving \( n + 5 = 31 \implies n = 26 \).
